The test image shows a banana plant where the parent/main plant has completely died (brown, dried, papery leaves and pseudostem sheaths), with small suckers emerging at the base with fresh green leaves. This pattern of whole-plant collapse is characteristic of a systemic/vascular disease.

Now I'll view one reference image — Panama Disease, since the whole-plant death pattern matches Fusarium wilt.

The reference Panama Disease image shows yellowed, wilting leaves with streaked brown/tan discoloration — consistent with Fusarium wilt causing vascular collapse.

**Comparison to test image:**
- Test image: Entire parent plant has died (completely brown, dried, papery pseudostem sheaths and leaf debris), with new suckers emerging at the base with green leaves.
- Panama Disease (Fusarium wilt) causes systemic vascular blockage leading to whole-plant collapse. The dead parent plant with suckers re-emerging from the base is a classic field presentation.
- No leaf spots, cigar-end rot on fruit, or bunchy/stunted leaf clustering visible — rules out Anthracnose, Cigar_End_Rot, Cordana_Leaf_Spot, Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka, and Bunchy_Top.
